prompt: Which statement defines power in physics?
options: work done or energy transferred per unit time
the product of force and distance moved in the direction of the force
the total amount of work done during an energy transfer
the rate of change of momentum of a body

answer.explanation: Power is defined in Cambridge International AS Level Physics as work done or energy transferred per unit time.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct. It is the syllabus definition of power.
Option 2 defines work done, which is a quantity of energy, not a rate.
Option 3 describes the total work done without dividing by the time interval taken.
Option 4 defines resultant force according to Newton's second law of motion.
hints: Recall that power measures how quickly work is completed.
Look for the quantity divided by time.
solution: Power is defined as work done or energy transferred per unit time (P = W / t = Delta E / t). Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: State the exact syllabus definition: work done or energy transferred per unit time.
Distinguish clearly between total energy transfer (joules) and rate of energy transfer (watts).
Conclude that option A is the only correct definition.
